universal_lens: The alignment of sparse highlight frames to continuous broadcast streams constitutes a constrained optimal transport problem. By minimizing the PSNR metric under strict temporal continuity constraints, we define a bi-Lipschitz mapping between disjoint video manifolds, effectively projecting high-dimensional visual features onto a unified, temporally coherent event space. TF-SELECTOR integrates shot boundary detection, ASR transcription, VLM captioning, and LLM saliency scoring into a modular pipeline for long-form sport video highlight detection.
gsi_mapping: Within GSI, PSNR acts as a localized likelihood function evaluating feature congruence across varying broadcast camera angles. The threshold τ functions as a conformal prediction boundary; alignments exceeding this residual variance are flagged as out-of-distribution, ensuring that only statistically robust spatiotemporal correspondences propagate into the global Bayesian inference engine. Bayesian belief updates on segment saliency scores using VLM captions and ASR transcripts enable probabilistic highlight inference in real-time video streams.
gse_mapping: For GSE, this primitive governs state-transition validation during multi-camera tracking. When an agent's trajectory is occluded in one feed but visible in another, the PSNR threshold enforces physical plausibility. It prevents discontinuous jumps in the situational graph, guaranteeing that reconstructed play-by-play states strictly adhere to kinematic limits. Situationally grounded state transitions from shot segments to highlighted clips are governed by LLM-derived saliency thresholds and multimodal input fusion.

reasoning_traces.think: The mathematical foundation of the SVHighlights pipeline rests upon the rigorous formulation of a constrained optimization problem over high-dimensional video manifolds. We conceptualize the highlight video and the full broadcast as two distinct topological spaces, $\mathcal{M}_H$ and $\mathcal{M}_F$, respectively. The core objective is to construct a bijective mapping $\phi: \mathcal{M}_H \rightarrow \mathcal{M}_F$ that preserves both semantic content and temporal ordering. The utilization of Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) as the primary alignment metric introduces a localized Euclidean distance measure in pixel space, $D(H_i, F_t) = \| H_i - F_t \|^2$. However, raw pixel-wise minimization is inherently prone to local minima caused by camera angle variations and broadcast overlays. To mitigate this, the authors introduce a temporal consistency constraint governed by the threshold $\tau$. This transforms the alignment from a purely spatial search into a spatio-temporal dynamic programming problem. The condition $| \text{PSNR}(f^*) - \text{PSNR}(f^+) | < \tau$ essentially penalizes trajectories that exhibit discontinuous jumps in the feature space, enforcing a Lipschitz continuity on the derived mapping. Furthermore, the explicit preservation of non-active gameplay segments (timeouts, replays) dictates that the domain of our mapping must be the entire continuous interval $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$, rather than a sparse subset of 'action' frames. This holistic approach ensures that the resulting aligned dataset retains the full causal structure of the sporting event, which is paramount for training robust, temporally-aware deep learning models capable of understanding complex, long-horizon dependencies in sports analytics.

This anti-collinearity check ensures that the feature vectors of consecutive frames remain within a bounded subspace. Leakage is prevented by explicitly isolating the pre- and post-game segments; by hard-clipping the analysis window to $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$, we eliminate the risk of correlating unrelated studio analyst footage with on-field actions, thereby maintaining the purity of the situational state graph.
